# Croff Electric: full business facts

Canonical page: https://diyregistry.com/s/croff-electric/
Facts checked: 2026-10-24. This is a RegisterMySite demo, not yet published by the business.

## Identity
- Name: Croff Electric
- Owner: Jeremy Croff (the CSLB record lists Jeremy Eugene Croff, sole ownership)
- Team: family-run. Reviewers describe a "father, sons" crew.
- Location: Long Beach, CA. Service-area business; the street address isn't published.
- Phone: (310) 406-6909
- Email: croffelectric@yahoo.com
- Languages: English

## Licenses
- California CSLB C-10 Electrical Contractor #1044752: current and active, issued 2018-09-24, expires 2028-09-30. Bonded for $25,000. Verify: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/OnlineServices/CheckLicenseII/LicenseDetail.aspx?LicNum=1044752
- City of Long Beach business license BU22104948 (Contracting – Electrical): active, renewed 2026-08-27.
- Listed as an in-network contractor in SCE's Charge Ready Home directory (updated 06/24/2026).

## Hours
- Monday–Saturday 7:00 AM–5:00 PM. Sunday closed. These are the hours on Yelp; Google shows Mon–Sat 8–5.
- No 24/7 emergency service.

## Services
- Hardwired Level 2 EV charger installation, including for SCE Charge Ready Home
- Electric panel upgrades, installation and repair; circuit breakers
- Rewiring older and historic homes
- Lighting: LED retrofits, can lights, fixtures
- Ceiling fans
- Outlets and switches; 240V circuits (stove, dryer, HVAC prep)
- Doorbells, generators
- Electrical inspection and troubleshooting
- Conduit prep for future solar

## Service area
- Long Beach and nearby communities, including Lakewood

## Estimates and payment
- Free estimates. Quotes are sometimes given over the phone.
- No published prices.
- Payment: credit card, Zelle, Venmo

## On-page tool
- EV Charger & Panel Readiness Planner. You enter charger amps, panel size, home age, existing big loads, distance and location. It shows a typical breaker and copper wire size (from the NEC 125% continuous-load rule) and a readiness tier: straightforward, load calc recommended, or panel upgrade likely. It's a rough guide only, with no prices, and you can send the summary with your free-estimate request.
